submission.natural_language_explanation: This head is NOT broad. It fires strongly (about 0.35-1.0 x max) on the comma that CLOSES a mid-sentence comma-delimited insertion: an appositive, a non-restrictive relative clause, a participial or prepositional aside, or a reporting tag. Examples are 'The mayor, who was elected last year[,]', 'X, a branch of the UN[,]' and 'suggested, amongst other things[,]'. From that closing comma it attends with weight about 1.0 back to the opening comma of the same sentence. Predict inactive (below 0.25 x max) for: opening commas; commas after sentence-initial intro words or phrases ('However,', 'In 2019,'); a comma whose insertion was opened by a dash, parenthesis or semicolon instead of a comma; insertions closed by a period or semicolon; and short comma-free 'The N V.' sentences and ordinary comma-free prose. In longer documents, phrase-final nouns and names, especially list items and words around 'and', can cross the line weakly (about 0.25-0.6 x max). The closing comma is weaker when the text opens with a bare name or pronoun ('John, who...', 'She said, however,').
